raw_case_text: A 35-year-old woman with no particular history was hospitalized for a headache, fever, jaundice (Figure 1(b)), and impaired consciousness after 2 days of quinine injection administered at her home. On admission, clinical examination indicated a fever of 39.6 C, a weight of 60 kg, a Glasgow score of 10, a respiratory rate of 31 cycles/minute, a thick negative peripheral blood smear, but a malaria RDT positive for P. falciparum. The hemoglobin concentration was 5 g/dl, and the blood glucose level was 3.9 mmol/L. Urinary catheter insertion revealed port wine-colored urine, which prompted the BWF diagnosis. The urine test strip indicated hemoglobinuria at 2 plus; bilirubinuria 3 plus; proteinuria 2 plus; absence of urobilinogens, red blood cells, and leukocytes; creatinemia of 450 mumol/L; and urea of 31.39 mmol; and quinine discontinuation was followed by treatment with intramuscularly injected artemether at a dose of 3.2 mg/kg daily on day 1 and 1.6 mg/kg daily from day 2 to day 5. The patient had three sessions of extrarenal purification and transfusion with 4,450 ml bags of blood. Evolution was favorable with clinical improvement and recovery of renal function after 5 days.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 35-year-old woman presented with headache, high fever, jaundice, port-wine-colored urine, and impaired consciousness after 2 days of home quinine injections.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: After receiving 2 days of parenteral quinine injections at home for a febrile illness, the patient was hospitalized with persistent fever, headache, jaundice, port-wine-colored urine, and altered sensorium.
subjective.past_medical_history: Unremarkable past medical history; received 2 days of home quinine injections prior to admission.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for headache, fever, jaundice, dark port-wine-colored urine, and impaired consciousness.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature 39.6 C, weight 60 kg, Glasgow Coma Scale score 10, RR 31 cycles/min, clinical jaundice, and port-wine-colored urine upon urinary catheterization.
objective.routine_investigations: Severe anemia with Hb 5 g/dL, blood glucose 3.9 mmol/L, serum creatinine 450 umol/L, and urea 31.39 mmol/L. Urine dipstick showed hemoglobinuria 2+, bilirubinuria 3+, proteinuria 2+, and no RBCs, WBCs, or urobilinogen.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Quinine-induced blackwater fever (BWF) with severe acute intravascular hemolysis (Hb 5 g/dL) and oliguric/azotemic acute kidney injury associated with Plasmodium falciparum malaria. Malaria RDT was positive for P. falciparum with a negative thick peripheral blood smear. Managed by immediate discontinuation of quinine, initiation of intramuscular artemether (3.2 mg/kg on day 1, then 1.6 mg/kg/day on days 2-5), 3 sessions of hemodialysis, and transfusion of four 450 mL units of whole blood, achieving full clinical and renal recovery within 5 days.
